steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Prepare the elbow macaroni according to package directions.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium high heat. Stir in the flour until a cream colored paste forms. Then pour in the milk and stir constantly until this comes to a hard boil, then stir for 1 more minute. Remove from heat and set aside.

When the macaroni is cooked, spread 1/2 of it into the bottom of a lightly greased 9x13-inch baking dish. Then layer 1/2 of the grated onion, 1/2 of the salt and pepper and 1/2 of each of the cheeses. Repeat this one more time: macaroni, onion, salt and pepper and cheeses, and then pour the reserved white sauce over all. Top off with small pats of butter to taste.
Cover and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Old Fashioned Mac and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This classic recipe for creamy baked macaroni and cheese uses three cheeses to create a family-friendly meal.
raw_recipe.name: Old Fashioned Mac and Cheese

review.reviewBody: Awesome!!! Just like Mom used to make!!! I have never rated a recipe before but one thing I noticed with the reviews...if you are going to rate the recipe make it the way it is written. One of the previous reviewers gave it a four because she changed it all over the place and obviously thought hers was better, I looked at other reviews she has done and has done the same thing to other recioes. Review it on it's merits, not on what you think you did to make it your own!

I LOVE THIS MAC & CHEESE and so does everyone else who has it, even the kids. I have made it countless times over the years and am always asked to make it for parties or bbqs. I initially followed the recipe to the letter and eventually just started experimenting with different cheeses because I love cheese. I have settled on Swiss, Gruyere, and triple cheddar. I also grind my onion in a food processor to make it with no crunch but all the flavor. Some that claim to hate onions don't know they are in there and love it lol. I use 1/2 heavy whipping cream and 1/2 whole milk. I had so many rave reviews, someone just asked me to make it for a party of 40! Sounds easy enough! Thanks for this great recipe! I have even used alternative dairy and other products for a healthier version but my go to is Fat Full, Gluten Full, and Dairy Full LOL

Yes, I melted the cheese and mixed it in with the white sauce.
Poured 1/2 over 1/2 of mac and then the mac and the sauce.
I also used gluten free pasta by Jovial and only cooked it 6 minutes so it would not get soggy!
I am not a cook, but. followed this recipe and it came out delicious. I also increased the cheese on top, because one can never have enough cheese, right?

This was a really good recipe. I liked the Swiss cheese and onions. I softened the onions a little in some butter, and didn't do the layering method. Just melted the cheeses into the warm milk/ flour. Next time I'll add a little more Velveeta for more creaminess and flavor. Also added a sleeve of crushed Ritz browned in butter for a little crunch on top.

I loved this recipe! I made exactly as written except for leaving out the onions (family preference) and I used the cheese I had on hand: sharp cheddar, mozzarella and swiss. I will experiment with other cheeses in the future. It is the best way to make mac and cheese, using the white sauce with layers of cheese. Fantastic! UPDATE: Having made this a few times, I now double the sauce and pour half the sauce over the bottom layer as I am assembling it. Makes it creamier. I also have tried a variation to cut carbs a little. I replace half the macaroni with cooked cauliflower chunks. I have also at times added a cup of cooked mixed vegetables. I love it this way! It's certainly not low carb or low cal, but it does help reduce the heavy carb load and honestly I can't tell the difference.

This is a creamy delicious recipe. It's not necessary to make changes. However, when I made the recipe, I wanted to first sautee the onions. In addition, in the last 5 minutes in the oven, I crumbled sour cream and onion potato chips as a topping and placed the dish under the broil for 3 minutes. These changes gave a little extra taste to an already yummy casserole.

This was the tastiest and creamiest Mac And y cheese! The only thing I did differently was to sauté the onions and some sweet yellow peppers before adding to the layers. It really thickens up and not so hard to make.
I made this as the recipe is written, unlike so many other reviews. It was ok. I much prefer melting the cheese into the roux and adding the macaroni to the cheese sauce.
I used medium shells and a mix of sharp cheddars and fontina. Also added heavy cream in place of some of the milk. This was decadent and delicious.
This recipe was SO good... everyone at our party loved it. Added 1/4 c Franks Red Hot to the white sauce for an extra kick!! This is a new staple recipe!

This was rich and cheesy. There was plenty of sauce for the macaroni. The onions basically vanished in the final product, but I also minced them very small so they would. I cooked the onion in with the butter and then just added the flour in once the onions were done to my liking. I didn't bother with all the layering since it's all going to melt down and become one sauce, so the cheese went into the white sauce and once it was all melted, I poured it over the macaroni in the dish. I scaled down to make 3 servings and this was finished baking in 29 minutes, not the 45 given. It was already a little overbaked. The cheese sauce was really nicely flavored, but that cheddar gave it a slightly grainy gritty texture, so maybe add more Velveeta and use a much sharper cheddar, but way less of it? I'd fix this again. It was a good mac and cheese. My husband missed the crunchy cracker topping that baked macaroni and cheese often has on it. I'll admit I did too. This is basic but tasty and filled us up.
Went with the recipe except added 1/2 cup heavy cream. This is a great recipe grate your cheese don’t use pregrated it is just not as good.
My kids love it and insist I make it every year for Thanksgiving. It's SO good!

A friend asked me to make macaroni and cheese. I remember my mom making it years ago and don’t think I’ve ever made this dish. I remember Velveeta, milk and macaroni and not much else. I found this recipe and loved the thought of a sauce. I didn’t have any Velveeta, don’t particularly care for it and wasn’t going to drive 10 miles to the store for processed cheese. I always have loads of cheese so decided to use a combination of sharp cheddar, Monterey Jack and havarati. I couldn’t quite wrap my head around the layering. After draining the macaroni I added 1 cup of pasta water back into the pot with the macaroni, added all the cheese and onion. I mixed it well, added salt and pepper and put it in a baking dish. Poured the cream sauce over, added a sprinkle of paprika and voila, perfect macaroni. Thank you JAYDE175 for a great recipe.

I made this for a potluck and it was a huge hit! Absolutely incredible recipe, my friends couldn’t get enough of it. I was a little bit short on butter, but I decided to replace it with a couple spoonfuls of shaving cream which added an extra level of creaminess that really elevated this dish. Will be making again!
Tasted good. Used onion powder instead of the grated onions. This recipe doesn't fill a 9x13 as written, so can use a smaller dish or double to fill.
Loved it! Added more Swiss, as thats our favorite cheese.
